\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ڈاکٹر} (ḍākṭar)}{ڈاکٹر (ḍākṭar)}]{\ur{ڈاکٹر} (ḍākṭar) — a doctor}

\label{lesson:UR-C471-daktar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a faint, then the Urdu for frailty.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ڈاکٹر}}
\textbf{\ur{ڈاکٹر}} — \emph{ḍākṭar} — \textquotedblleft{}a doctor\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ڈاکٹر} \ur{نے} \ur{مجھے} \ur{دوا} \ur{دی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ḍākṭar ne mujhe davā dī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The doctor gave me some medicine.
\end{quote}

Masculine or feminine, by the person meant.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ڈاکٹر}} (\emph{ḍākṭar}) is borrowed from English \emph{doctor}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍākṭar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍākṭar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍākṭar ne mujhe davā dī.} — The doctor gave me some medicine.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a faint, then the Urdu for frailty, then say \emph{ḍākṭar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{ڈاکٹر} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A doctor\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{صحت} (sehat)}{صحت (sehat)}]{\ur{صحت} (sehat) — health}

\label{lesson:UR-C471-sehat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for frailty, then the Urdu for a doctor.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{صحت}}
\textbf{\ur{صحت}} — \emph{sehat} — \textquotedblleft{}health\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ورزش} \ur{صحت} \ur{کے} \ur{لیے} \ur{اچھی} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{varzish sehat ke liye achchhī hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Exercise is good for your health.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{صحت}} (\emph{sehat}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ṣiḥḥa}, \textquotedblleft{}health, soundness\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for describing what you lived and felt.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{طبی} (tibbī)}{طبی (tibbī)}]{\ur{طبی} (tibbī) — medical}

\label{lesson:UR-C471-tibbi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for an ailment, then the Urdu for healing.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{طبی}}
\textbf{\ur{طبی}} — \emph{tibbī} — \textquotedblleft{}medical\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\ur{طبی}} (\emph{tibbī}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ṭibbī}, \textquotedblleft{}medical\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{ṭibb}, \textquotedblleft{}medicine\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.

\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from Inside the Body to Health}

\label{lesson:UR-R471-review-464-471}



\begin{quote}
Say the Urdu for the brain and a kidney.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item the brain, a kidney, the stomach as an organ, an intestine, a vein
  \item a bone, a rib, a skull, the backbone, a jaw
  \item an arm, a thigh, the calf of the leg, the sole of the foot, a paw
  \item the palate, a gum, to lick, to suck, to spit
  \item a scent, perfume, the sense of touch, to scratch an itch, a rash
  \item a burp, a hiccup, to clear one's throat, phlegm, catarrh
  \item to swell up, stamina, to break into a sweat, a faint, frailty
  \item a doctor, health, an ailment, healing, medical
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
The brain? (\textbf{\ur{دماغ}}, \emph{dimāgh}.) A kidney? (\textbf{\ur{گردہ}}, \emph{gurdā}.) The stomach as an organ? (\textbf{\ur{معدہ}}, \emph{medā}.) An intestine? (\textbf{\ur{آنت}}, \emph{āṅt}.) A vein? (\textbf{\ur{رگ}}, \emph{rag}.) A bone? (\textbf{\ur{ہڈی}}, \emph{haḍḍī}.) A rib? (\textbf{\ur{پسلی}}, \emph{paslī}.) A skull? (\textbf{\ur{کھوپڑی}}, \emph{khopṛī}.) The backbone? (\textbf{\ur{ریڑھ}}, \emph{rīṛh}.) A jaw? (\textbf{\ur{جبڑا}}, \emph{jabṛā}.) An arm? (\textbf{\ur{بازو}}, \emph{bāzū}.) A thigh? (\textbf{\ur{ران}}, \emph{rān}.) The calf of the leg? (\textbf{\ur{پنڈلی}}, \emph{pinḍlī}.) The sole of the foot? (\textbf{\ur{تلوا}}, \emph{talvā}.) A paw? (\textbf{\ur{پنجہ}}, \emph{panjā}.) The palate? (\textbf{\ur{تالو}}, \emph{tālū}.) A gum? (\textbf{\ur{مسوڑھا}}, \emph{masūṛhā}.) To lick? (\textbf{\ur{چاٹنا}}, \emph{chāṭnā}.) To suck? (\textbf{\ur{چوسنا}}, \emph{chūsnā}.) To spit? (\textbf{\ur{تھوکنا}}, \emph{thūknā}.) A scent? (\textbf{\ur{مہک}}, \emph{mahak}.) Perfume? (\textbf{\ur{عطر}}, \emph{itr}.) The sense of touch? (\textbf{\ur{لمس}}, \emph{lams}.) To scratch an itch? (\textbf{\ur{کھجانا}}, \emph{khujānā}.) A rash? (\textbf{\ur{خارش}}, \emph{khārish}.) A burp? (\textbf{\ur{ڈکار}}, \emph{ḍakār}.) A hiccup? (\textbf{\ur{ہچکی}}, \emph{hichkī}.) To clear one's throat? (\textbf{\ur{کھنکارنا}}, \emph{khaṅkārnā}.) Phlegm? (\textbf{\ur{بلغم}}, \emph{balgham}.) Catarrh? (\textbf{\ur{نزلہ}}, \emph{nazlā}.) To swell up? (\textbf{\ur{پھولنا}}, \emph{phūlnā}.) Stamina? (\textbf{\ur{دم}}, \emph{dam}.) To break into a sweat? (\textbf{\ur{پسیجنا}}, \emph{pasījnā}.) A faint? (\textbf{\ur{غش}}, \emph{ghash}.) Frailty? (\textbf{\ur{نقاہت}}, \emph{naqāhat}.) A doctor? (\textbf{\ur{ڈاکٹر}}, \emph{ḍākṭar}.) Health? (\textbf{\ur{صحت}}, \emph{sehat}.) An ailment? (\textbf{\ur{مرض}}, \emph{marz}.) Healing? (\textbf{\ur{شفا}}, \emph{shifā}.) Medical? (\textbf{\ur{طبی}}, \emph{tibbī}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
